currentContext.expansion: HBL operates seven manufacturing plants and 22 offices in India, with integrated facilities at Vizianagaram (2V/12V AGM VRLA), Shamirpet (Ni-Cd, specialty batteries and power electronics), Nandigaon (PLT, lithium-ion and submarine batteries), Thumkunta (electronics), Visakhapatnam SEZ (Ni-Cd batteries) and a development centre at Yapral. Following 100% growth in data centre sales, PLT production capacity is being doubled. Nickel cadmium capacity is being expanded for both domestic and export markets, with a strong FY27 order book flow necessitating further capacity expansion. For defence lithium-ion, HBL has invested about Rs 200 crores for R&D and a modern production plant adequate for foreseeable demand, with technology licensed from NSTL of DRDO and no foreign collaboration; plant capacity can be increased by line balancing if needed. A licensed facility for the manufacturing of electronic fuzes has been established in Telangana. In electric drive trains, HBL assembled a few 55 T trucks for on-road demonstration and has completed about 40,000 km of internal road trials; kit parts and the assembled truck are expected to complete homologation approvals by March 2027, with pilot sales from July 2027, a nine-month delay caused by the redesign to magnet-less motors after permanent-magnet supply-chain hurdles. Marine drive trains require batteries, motors and electronics to marine standards, which will take a year, with sales limited until end September 2027. On March 25, 2026 HBL signed a JV agreement with Cochin Shipyard Limited for marine electric mobility and energy storage, taking 60% of the JV; Green Maritime Propulsion Private Limited was incorporated at Hyderabad on June 11, 2026 with authorised and subscribed capital of Rs 9 crores, and has already placed an order on HBL for batteries for two electric tugs. On the sustainability side, during FY2025-26 the Company invested INR 2.33 crore in a solar power system and a 600 KVA DG set at its Vizag facility and INR 6.7 crore in 1.2 MW and 1.0 MW solar power plants at Nandigaon, and commissioned an 80 KLD Multiple Effect Evaporator for water recycling.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: HBL Engineering Limited (formerly HBL Power Systems) is an engineering-intensive Indian manufacturer that identifies and fills technology gaps in-house, operating nine business units across three segments — Industrial Electronics, Industrial Batteries and Defence.

business_model.title: Business (RHP)
business_model.body: HBL organizes engineering talent to identify technology gaps in India that it can fill, and manufactures engineering-intensive products to grow profitably. Its three segments are Industrial Electronics (rail signalling — Kavach and TMS/CTC, electric drive trains, other industrial electronics), Industrial Batteries (lead acid, nickel cadmium and lithium-ion) and Defence (batteries for aircraft, missiles, torpedoes, submarines and armoured vehicles, electronic fuzes, and special defence products). It sells to system integrators, EPC firms, and railway, aviation and defence customers in India …

capex_expansion.body: HBL operates seven manufacturing plants and 22 offices in India, with integrated facilities at Vizianagaram (2V/12V AGM VRLA), Shamirpet (Ni-Cd, specialty batteries and power electronics), Nandigaon (PLT, lithium-ion and submarine batteries), Thumkunta (electronics), Visakhapatnam SEZ (Ni-Cd batteries) and a development centre at Yapral. Following 100% growth in data centre sales, PLT production capacity is being doubled. Nickel cadmium capacity is being expanded for both domestic and export markets, with a strong FY27 order book flow necessitating further capacity expansion. For defence …

strategy.body:

themes.title: Renewable IPP / FDRE firm-power & storage
themes.need: DISCOMs mandating firm/round-the-clock RE make BESS + pumped-hydro the bid differentiator, and in Q1FY27 storage demand ran ahead of supply. ADANIGREEN has 3.5 GWh of BESS installed (+1.9 GWh at Khavda this quarter), targets 10+ GWh this fiscal and 50 GWh by FY30 on a thumb-rule INR 25-30 lakh of EBITDA per MWh against ~INR 1.5cr/MWh of capex, and has contracted essentially all merchant/C&I capacity to sibling AESL on 25-year (solar/wind) and 15-year (battery) fixed-price PPAs targeting ~15-16% IRR - a pivot from merchant builder to fixed-return contracted IPP, with evacuation (not panels) named as the binding constraint. JSWENERGY added 873 MW in Q1 and ~1.1 GW since April - 36% of its 3 GW FY27 target already banked, Tidong Hydro commissioned four months early - and raised INR 10,150cr, taking net leverage 5.2x to 4.95x. On the equipment side SERVOTECH said its BESS pack capacity is fully booked ('we are not able to meet the demand') and committed to 2x capacity in 6 months, 3x by 21-Mar-2027 and 10x within 2 years. ACMESOLAR/KPIGREEN/SUZLON/INOXWIND attach storage to solar/wind; NTPC/NHPC/SJVN/TATAPOWER drive pumped-hydro and utility-scale storage.
themes.driver: BESS capacity commissioning against demand two independent managements (ADANIGREEN, SERVOTECH) say already exceeds supply; FDRE/peak-power tender awards; merchant DAM prices (JSWENERGY: INR 4.40 -> INR 5.10/unit, +16%) on +8.5% Q1 power demand.
